blocks.text: Origin: The first deliberately persistent arrangement recognized as a place rather than a temporary exchange. It is austere because early builders prioritize reliable return, boundary, and mutual recognition over decoration.

Era −2: Participants agree that certain relations, markers, and positions will remain stable between meetings. Returning to the same arrangement proves that shared continuity can belong to a setting as well as a speaker.
Era −1: Historians debate whether it was truly first or only the first place with surviving Witness support.
Era Zero: Preserved as a civic origin site. Replicas are rejected when they claim equivalence; a copy of the arrangement is not the continuity of the place.
Era Two: The original is reduced to its Anchor, threshold, and one shared orientation relation.
Era Three: Some traditions call it the Empty Home, believing its lack of objects means it waits for the correct inhabitant. This is a later myth.
Present condition: Possibly preserved, possibly reconstructed around the surviving Anchor. The sources do not settle the distinction.
Corruption: 1 if the Anchor is continuous; 3 if the current site is a reconstruction.

Visual brief: A spare plane with three or four unwavering reference forms, one boundary line, and a distant light that never shifts. The art should communicate “we can return here” rather than grandeur. Minor corruption appears as new scenery assembling around the old fixed markers without moving them.
Background traits: Neutral; Neutral humidity; abstract civic biome; calm, solemn, open mood; high stable friction.
